ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md`. The skill requires this before every fix round. It decides whether I resume the implementer or start a fresh subagent, and how the re-review runs.

ACTION: Dispatch a fix subagent on model `sonnet` (resumed or fresh, as fix-loop.md says). Its purpose is to fix F1 in Task 4. It gets the Task 4 brief, the global constraints, and F1 verbatim. It first writes a failing test in `tests/test_retry.py` that asserts the exact retry count equals the configured `max_retries`. Then it changes `attempt > max_retries` to `attempt >= max_retries` at `fetch/retry.py:41`. Then it runs the tests, commits, and reports.

F1 is a one-character fix, but I sent it to a fix subagent. I did not edit it myself.

Your rule says to fix tiny things directly. The skill lets me do that only when the change alters no behavior, such as a typo or wording. Changing `>` to `>=` changes how many retries the client makes, so it counts as a code change. That holds even for one character.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The current test only asserts that a retry happens, not how many. That gap let the off-by-one pass. The subagent will add a test on the exact count, written to fail first, so the fix is proven and the bug stays caught.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

When the subagent reports, I will generate the diff file and run a scoped re-review of F1. If it comes back clean, I will log Task 4 as complete and move to the next task.
